'''Matthew William Choptuik''' (born 1961) is a Canadian theoretical physicist specializing in numerical relativity.

Choptuik graduated from [[University of British Columbia]] with a master's degree in 1982 and a Ph.D. advised by [[William Unruh]] in 1986. He became an associate professor in 1995 at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. In 1999 he became a member of the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics|Institute for Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] and in the same year he became a professor at University of British Columbia.

In 1993,<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9 | title=Universality and scaling in gravitational collapse of a massless scalar field | date=1993 | last1=Choptuik | first1=Matthew W. | journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=70 | issue=1 | pages=9–12 | pmid=10053245 | bibcode=1993PhRvL..70....9C | url-access=subscription }}</ref> he discovered critical phenomena in gravitational collapse<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.12942/lrr-2007-5 | doi-access=free | title=Critical Phenomena in Gravitational Collapse | date=2007 | last1=Gundlach | first1=Carsten | last2=Martín-García | first2=José M. | journal=Living Reviews in Relativity | volume=10 | issue=1 | page=5 | pmid=28179820 | pmc=5256106 | arxiv=0711.4620 | bibcode=2007LRR....10....5G }}</ref> via numerical studies. He showed—under non-generic initial conditions <ref>Only with precise fine tuning of the initial conditions, which is lost even with small perturbations</ref>—the possibility of the occurrence of [[naked singularity]] in general relativity with scalar matter. This had previously been the subject of a bet between [[Stephen Hawking]], [[Kip Thorne]] and [[John Preskill]]. Hawking lost the bet after Choptuik's publication, but renewed it under non-generic initial conditions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Crenson |first=Matt |title=The naked truth: Astrophysicist Stephen Hawking loses a bet |url=https://www.apnews.com/7e02e4d3e6c9cc569aeb229e0e47efaf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190512162621/https://www.apnews.com/7e02e4d3e6c9cc569aeb229e0e47efaf |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 12, 2019 |work=AP News |date=February 12, 1997}}</ref>

Choptuik was the 2001 awardee of the [[Rutherford Memorial Medal]]. In 2003 he received the [[CAP-CRM Prize in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics]]. In 2003 he became a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. In 2002, he became an honorary doctor of Brandon University.
